atlas-pl.0001: Europe’s largest market for business-service centres: about 489,000 people work in 2,081 centres run by foreign and Polish firms, mostly in Warsaw, Kraków and Wrocław, many in Western European languages. Entry pay is modest and automation is thinning the junior rung. Non-EU graduates of Polish universities get nine months to find work.

atlas-pl.0015: Client-facing banking and consulting entry in Warsaw is unresearched.
atlas-pl.0016: At the end of Q1 2025, 488,700 people worked in 2,081 business-service centres in Poland; Warsaw has 429 centres, Kraków 324 and Wrocław 258, and Warsaw and Kraków each employ more than 100,000.
atlas-pl.0017: Kraków’s service centres employed nearly 108,000 people in Q1 2025, and new centres opened in Poland since 2024 were mostly in IT (42.6%) and R&D (26.2%).
atlas-pl.0018: HSBC’s Kraków centre covers risk, business analysis and IT application support across 27 countries and works in 11 languages, including Italian, German and French.
atlas-pl.0019: Goldman Sachs uses Warsaw as a technology and engineering base.
atlas-pl.0020: Bending Spoons opened a Warsaw office in September 2026 and received about 50,000 applications from Poland in the first nine months of 2026.
atlas-pl.0021: Foreigners are 19.6% of centre staff, and Italians 8.3% of those; most centres pay a monthly language allowance of PLN 600 to 2,000.
atlas-pl.0022: 74.1% of centres use intelligent process automation, and Big Four partners in Poland describe junior transactional roles shrinking.
atlas-pl.0023: A junior specialist in a Polish centre earned a mean base of €1,744 a month in 2024; at the average wage a single worker keeps 71.7% of gross.
atlas-pl.0024: On that pay, a central one-bed leaves about €190 a month in Warsaw and about €500 in Wrocław.

atlas-pl.0037: Eurostat counts 1,186,600 people in work in the Katowice metropolitan region in 2021: 49,400 in information and communication (third in Poland, after Warsaw and Kraków) and 31,600 in finance and insurance (second in Poland, after Warsaw). The region’s GDP was €44.6 billion in 2021.
atlas-pl.0038: Eurostat counts 657,000 people in work in the Gdańsk metropolitan region in 2021: 32,000 in information and communication and 20,000 in finance and insurance. The region’s GDP was €23.8 billion in 2021.
atlas-pl.0039: Eurostat counts 701,400 people in work in the Poznań metropolitan region in 2021: 26,800 in information and communication and 18,700 in finance and insurance. The region’s GDP was €28.6 billion in 2021.
atlas-pl.0040: Eurostat counts 545,400 people in work in the Łódź metropolitan region in 2021: 23,200 in information and communication and 15,000 in finance and insurance. The region’s GDP was €18.4 billion in 2021.
atlas-pl.0041: No family is rated in Gdańsk, Poznań or Łódź: the Eurostat figures read do not put them second or third in the country for finance or information-and-communication jobs.
atlas-pl.0042: Warsaw, Kraków, Wrocław and Katowice are rated from Eurostat’s 2021 metropolitan employment counts and ABSL’s 2025 centre counts; ABSL’s functional split by city, and its 2026 report (Q1 2026), were not read, so finance, accounting and IT are not rated separately inside the centres.
atlas-pl.0043: Named employers outside the service-centre sector (banks, PKO Bank Polski, Allegro, Comarch, InPost) could not be placed in a city from their own pages and are not listed; the Warsaw Stock Exchange’s own page gives no listing count.
atlas-pl.0044: Gdańsk, Poznań and Łódź carry a standing for IT but no demand rating: the Eurostat counts put them fifth to seventh in the country.

atlas-pl.0047: the largest exchange in Central and Eastern Europe
atlas-pl.0050: Eurostat counts 119,200 people employed in information and communication in the Warsaw metropolitan region in 2021, 24% of Poland’s 496,800 and fourth among the 25 European capital regions reported, and 113,800 in finance and insurance, 28% of 405,700 and second among them after Paris.
atlas-pl.0051: Eurostat counts 65,800 people employed in information and communication in the Kraków metropolitan region in 2021 (13% of Poland’s, second after Warsaw) and 28,600 in finance and insurance, out of 844,400 in work.
atlas-pl.0052: Eurostat counts 47,800 people employed in information and communication in the Wrocław metropolitan region in 2021, fourth in Poland after Warsaw, Kraków and Katowice, and 24,200 in finance and insurance, out of 434,400 in work.
atlas-pl.0053: In 2025 ICT specialists were 4.5% of employment in Poland (778,800 people), against 5.0% in the EU.
atlas-pl.0054: In 2025 the average monthly gross wage in Poland was PLN 9,371; in the city counties it was PLN 11,678 in Warsaw, 11,404 in Kraków, 10,956 in Gdańsk, 10,794 in Katowice, 10,285 in Poznań, 10,148 in Wrocław and 9,367 in Łódź.
atlas-pl.0055: The Warsaw Stock Exchange says it is the largest stock exchange of financial instruments in Central and Eastern Europe and has the biggest capitalisation of all exchanges in the region.
atlas-pl.0056: The Global Financial Centres Index 40 (September 2026) ranks Warsaw 78th of 117 centres and third in Eastern Europe and Central Asia, after Astana and Cyprus; for fintech it is 87th. Kraków is not listed.
atlas-pl.0057: Startup Genome’s 2026 report puts the Warsaw ecosystem’s value at $3 billion and Kraków’s at $1 billion, against a European average of $14.3 billion.
atlas-pl.0058: Bolt names Warsaw among its four key hubs, with London, Bucharest and Berlin, around its Tallinn headquarters.
atlas-pl.0059: CD PROJEKT RED S.A. gives its registered seat as ul. Jagiellońska 74, Warsaw.
atlas-pl.0060: In 2025, 91.2% of Polish tertiary graduates aged 20–34 who finished within the last three years were in work (EU 85.3%), unemployment among 15-to-24-year-olds was 12.2% (EU 15.2%, Poland 11.4% in 2023) and 45.2% of 25-to-34-year-olds had a tertiary degree (EU 44.8%).
atlas-pl.0061: PKO Bank Polski opened recruitment for the second edition of its paid branch internship on 7 May 2026; the internship ran from 1 July to 30 September 2026 in branches in 20 cities.
atlas-pl.0062: KPMG Poland’s World of Audit held workshops on 8, 15 and 22 October and guarantees those who complete them a paid full-time audit internship starting in January; recruitment to the programme has ended for this year.
atlas-pl.0063: PwC Poland’s three-month All-Techclusive internship runs from early July to the end of September; recruitment for summer 2026 has closed.
atlas-pl.0064: The University of Warsaw’s autumn 2026 fairs are Psychological Career Days on 13 to 15 October, the Faculty of Management career day on 20 and 21 October and an IT job fair on 28 October; past years also had spring fairs in March and a public-sector day in May.
atlas-pl.0065: Poland’s largest door for graduates is the business-services sector: 2,081 centres run by foreign and Polish firms employed 488,700 people in early 2025, mostly in Warsaw and Kraków, and they hire juniors in volume, often for their languages. Polish banks, the Big Four and industry recruit through internships and programmes for students still at university.
atlas-pl.0066: Students work early and cheaply for employers: a student under 26 on a commission contract (umowa zlecenie) costs no social or health contributions, and income up to PLN 85,528 a year is free of income tax for everyone under 26.
atlas-pl.0068: Finance, risk, IT and customer operations for multinationals; a European language plus English is a paid skill, worth an allowance of about PLN 600 to 2,000 a month. Foreigners were 19.6% of the workforce, and Italians 8.3% of the foreigners.
atlas-pl.0069: ABSL counts foreign-owned centres at 84.3% of the employment and intelligent automation in more than 74% of centres, so the entry rung is thinner than the headcount suggests.
atlas-pl.0070: Paid internships at banks and the Big Four
atlas-pl.0071: PKO Bank Polski’s three-month paid internship for students and graduates ran from 1 July to 30 September 2026 in branches in 20 cities, and the bank says over 60% of interns continue working with it; KPMG’s World of Audit guarantees a paid full-time audit internship from January to those who complete three October workshops.
atlas-pl.0072: PwC runs a three-month summer programme in technology from July to September, with four recruitment stages (application, competency tests, language verification and an assessment centre); EY takes interns into audit and tax, with online tests for students and graduates before the interviews.
